methodologyNotes: Roster covers 12 current golf launch monitors and simulator front-ends spanning photometric (camera), radar, and hybrid Fusion-Tracking designs, from sub-$700 personal units to $16k tour-grade systems. Prices and headline specs were independently re-verified in this pass against manufacturer/official-store pages (skytrakgolf.com, bushnellgolf.com, garmin.com newsroom, foresightsports.com, shopindoorgolf.com and golfbays.com as authorized Uneekor dealers, fullswinggolf.com, rapsodo.com, flightscope.com). priceUsd is the base-unit MSRP/regular US price as currently listed (frequently discounted; see priceNote for sale/config context); bundled software, mats, screens and impact-screen packages are excluded unless noted. stated_accuracy is null for EVERY product: none of these brands publishes a formal manufacturer +/- tolerance, so qualitative or third-party comparative claims are quoted in provenance rather than carried in the spec field. The Garmin R10's draft accuracy block (club/ball speed and launch/carry tolerances) was NOT present in the cited Garmin press release and could not be corroborated, so it was removed (null beats a guess). releaseDate is null where no source reliably dated the launch. accessedAt 2026-08-16.

products.name: SkyTrak+
products.priceNote: MSRP per skytrakgolf.com; listed on sale at $1,995 in manufacturer sales
products.provenance: Re-verified on the official SkyTrak product page: $2,995 MSRP (listed on sale at $1,995), dual Doppler radar + photometric camera hybrid, club and spin metrics, Wi-Fi 2.4GHz, and a paid Membership required beyond the 14-day trial. SkyTrak publishes no formal +/- tolerance; the site's own third-party marketing claim (GolfBays: 'within ~2 yards of $20k+ monitors') is qualitative only, so stated_accuracy is null. releaseDate left null as no source verified the launch date.

products.name: Bushnell Golf Launch Pro (Circle B Edition)
products.priceNote: MSRP, Circle B Edition, indoor+outdoor with club+ball tracking
products.provenance: Re-verified on the official bushnellgolf.com page: the current unit is the 'Circle B Edition Launch Pro' at $2,999.99, an auto-calibrating three-camera infrared photometric system. Ball data works out of the box; full club data / more courses require the Silver ($199/yr) or Gold ($499/yr) subscription, with a 14-day Gold trial included. No manufacturer +/- accuracy figure is published (independent testers cite ~2% vs GCQuad, not a Bushnell spec), so stated_accuracy and releaseDate are null.

products.name: Garmin Approach R10
products.provenance: Release date (August 10, 2021) and launch MSRP ($599.99) confirmed via Garmin's own newsroom press release. The draft's specific accuracy tolerances (club head speed +/-5 mph, ball speed +/-1 mph, launch angle/direction +/-1 deg, carry +/-5 yards) do NOT appear in the cited press release and could not be corroborated as a Garmin-published spec, so stated_accuracy is set to null (null beats a guess). No ongoing subscription is required for core launch-monitor or Home Tee Hero use.

products.name: Garmin Approach R50
products.provenance: Re-verified via Garmin's newsroom release: announced November 12, 2024, suggested retail starting at $4,999.99, three-camera photometric system tracking 15+ ball/club metrics including measured spin rate and spin axis, with a built-in 10-inch touchscreen and Home Tee Hero simulator. Garmin Golf Premium is required for full simulator play; core launch data works without it. Garmin publishes no formal +/- accuracy figure, so stated_accuracy is null.

products.name: Foresight Sports GC3
products.priceNote: MSRP, starting price, base config with FSX Play
products.provenance: 'Starting at $6,999' confirmed on the official Foresight Sports GC3 page. Triscopic 3-camera photometric system; FSX Play ships with the unit and no subscription is required for core play (GSPro integration needs a separate ~$250/yr license). No manufacturer +/- accuracy figure is published (third-party testing cites ~1-2 mph ball speed vs GCQuad) and no verifiable release date was found, so stated_accuracy and releaseDate are null.

products.name: Foresight Sports GCQuad
products.provenance: $15,999 and the quadrascopic 4-camera photometric design confirmed on the official Foresight Sports GCQuad page ('world's most accurate, versatile and complete launch monitor'). Ships with FSX Play and courses at no ongoing cost. 'Most accurate' is a marketing claim, not a published +/- number, and no verifiable release date/year was found, so stated_accuracy and releaseDate are null.

products.name: Uneekor EYE XO2
products.priceNote: MSRP via authorized dealer (Uneekor sells through a dealer network, not direct)
products.provenance: $10,999 base price and the three high-speed infrared camera / non-marking-ball design confirmed on authorized dealer shopindoorgolf.com (Uneekor does not sell direct). Overhead-mounted, indoor-only; base impact-video camera included. Free 'Player' tier covers basic data, while GSPro/E6/GameDay compatibility and advanced tools require paid tiers. No manufacturer +/- accuracy figure or verified release year found, so stated_accuracy and releaseDate are null.

products.name: Uneekor QED
products.priceNote: MSRP, base package with bracket, marked balls, View software, per authorized dealer
products.provenance: $6,000 base price, dual-camera marked-ball design, and in-stock availability confirmed on authorized dealer golfbays.com. Refine/Refine+ software tiers are one-time purchases, not recurring subscriptions, so subscription_for_full_features is false. Fixed overhead mount makes it indoor-only. No manufacturer +/- accuracy figure or verified release year found ('within 1% of Trackman' is a qualitative reviewer claim only), so stated_accuracy and releaseDate are null.

products.name: Full Swing KIT
products.priceNote: MSRP, includes radar unit, travel case, charger, E6 Connect Perpetual Package
products.provenance: $4,999 MSRP, 24GHz Dual-Mode ML-enhanced radar plus 1080p camera, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth 5.0, and 2022 launch are well-established for the Full Swing KIT (endorsed/used by Tiger Woods). The official /kit-specs/ page geo-redirects for non-US visitors but is the canonical US source; golf.com corroborates the price and 16-metric data set. Core app data is free; course simulation is a separate paid package. No manufacturer +/- accuracy figure is published, so stated_accuracy is null.

products.name: Rapsodo MLM2PRO

specs.tracking_technology: photometric + radar (dual optical camera + Doppler radar)

products.provenance: Re-verified on the official Rapsodo page: $699.99 MSRP (listed on sale at $599.99), dual optical cameras plus Doppler radar, video feedback on all shots. Full accuracy/premium spin needs RPT-marked balls; a 45-day Premium trial precedes the paid subscription required for full simulator features. Rapsodo's 'within ~1%' claim is a comparative marketing statement, not a formal +/- spec, so stated_accuracy is null; no verifiable release year found, so releaseDate is null.

products.name: FlightScope Mevo+
products.priceNote: MSRP; listed on sale at $1,099 as FlightScope transitions the lineup to Mevo Gen2
products.provenance: Re-verified on the official FlightScope Mevo+ page: $2,299 regular price (listed on sale at $1,099), Fusion Tracking (radar+camera), built-in swing-video camera, and core data parameters always free with no subscription (optional Pro Package / Face Impact Location add-ons exist). Includes a 12-course E6 Connect bundle. No manufacturer +/- accuracy spec or verified release year was found, so stated_accuracy and releaseDate are null.

products.name: FlightScope Mevo Gen2
products.priceNote: MSRP; launched at $1,199 (Aug 2025), current listed price $1,299
products.provenance: Product confirmed real on the official FlightScope Mevo Gen2 page at $1,299 current price; FlightScope's own news post confirms it was announced August 4, 2025 at a $1,199 launch price. Fusion Tracking (3D Doppler radar + synchronized image processing), built-in camera, self-hosted Wi-Fi, and no subscription for core data. The 'within 1% of GCQuad / Trackman 4' figure is a third-party reviewer claim, not a manufacturer +/- spec, so stated_accuracy is null.
